referenceFunction.generalComment: This dataset represents the activity of waste disposal of spent anion exchange resin from potable water production in a municipal solid waste incinerator (MSWI) Recommended use of this dataset: disposal of used ion exchange resins *for potable water production*. Resins used of other purifications can have significantly more toxic composition, depending on use. Waste composition (wet, in ppm): upper heating value 16.06 MJ/kg; lower heating value 6.081 MJ/kg; H2O 499710; O 70320; H 40160; C 327130; S 23980; N 28640; P 10; B n.a.; Cl 7880; Br n.a.; F n.a.; I n.a.; Ag n.a.; As n.a.; Ba n.a.; Cd 1.592; Co n.a.; Cr n.a.; Cu 16.311; Hg n.a.; Mn n.a.; Mo n.a.; Ni n.a.; Pb 9.2482; Sb n.a.; Se n.a.; Sn 226.21; V n.a.; Zn 34.545; Be n.a.; Sc n.a.; Sr n.a.; Ti n.a.; Tl n.a.; W n.a.; Si 1880; Fe n.a.; Ca n.a.; Al n.a.; K n.a.; Mg n.a.; Na n.a.; Share of carbon in waste that is biogenic 0%. Share of metals in waste not oxidised and bulk-recyclable (exclude very small or thin parts) Iron: 0%; Alu: 0%; Copper: 0%. One kg of this waste produces 0.05049 kg of slag and 0.02777 kg of residues, which are landfilled. Additional solidification with 0.01111 kg of cement. Net energy production: 0.5MJ/kg electric energy and 1.18MJ/kg thermal energy. Recovery of metal scrap to recycling: 0g iron scrap, 0g aluminium scrap, 0g copper scrap.;; UUID: 6a15f966-125d-41cf-9a1f-ff3677bf589e
referenceFunction.includedProcesses: Waste incineration from waste reception gate further downstream (excluding transport to the MSWI plant). Waste-specific air and water emisions from incineration, auxiliary material consumption for flue gas cleaning. Short-term emissions to river water and long-term emisisons to ground water from slag compartment (from bottom ash) and residual material landfill (from solidified fly ashes and scrubber slugde). Waste-specific process energy demands for MSWI and net energy generation.

geography.text: Specific to the technology mix encountered in Switzerland in 2010. Well applicable to modern incineration practices in Europe, North America or Japan.

technology.text: average Swiss MSWI plants in 2010 (grate incinerators) with electrostatic precipitator for fly ash (ESP), wet flue gas scrubber and 25% SNCR , 42.77% SCR-high dust , 32.68% SCR-low dust -DeNOx facilities and 0% without Denox (weighted according to mass of burnt waste, representing Swiss average). Efficiency of iron scrap separation from slag : 58%. Efficiency of non-ferrous scrap separation from slag : 31%. Gross electric efficiency technology mix 15.84% and Gross thermal efficiency technology mix 28.51%

timePeriod.text: Waste composition as given in literature reference, theoretical data or other source. Transfer coefficients for modern MSWI.

representativeness.extrapolations: Typical elemental transfer coefficients from current studies for modern MSWI, completed with data from coal power plants and estimates, adapted for inert/burnable waste.
representativeness.samplingProcedure: fully waste-specific calculation based on literature data for average MSWI operation performance
representativeness.uncertaintyAdjustments: uncertainty of waste input composition data derived from generic formula GSD(c) = N*ln(c)+1
